name: Tilly
tagline: Asks the question nobody thought of.
bio: Tilly, a small brown owl: soft mottled brown and buff feathers with a paler speckled chest, large round amber-gold eyes, tufted ears, a small grey-black hooked beak and a calm, gently knowing expression; she is roughly the same height as Nibs
invariants: soft mottled brown and buff feathers, with a distinctly paler speckled chest
large round amber-gold eyes, set forward
a calm, gently knowing expression rather than a wide or startled one
child-sized: roughly the same height as Nibs the squirrel
both wings and her tail fully inside the frame, never cut by an edge
forbidden: a snowy, white, grey or barred owl; she is mottled brown and buff
yellow, orange or black eyes; they are amber-gold
a smooth round head with no ear tufts
a large, imposing or predatory owl; she is small and child-sized
a wide-eyed startled or comic expression; her calm is the point of her
Tilly wearing clothing, glasses, a hat or accessories
a realistic or anatomically detailed bird of prey; she is a soft storybook owl
talons drawn as weapons, or any suggestion of hunting
habit: she settles onto a branch and tilts her head a little before she says anything
notes: Tilly existed as reference art and a bio inside Nibs and the Absolutely Perfect
Acorn for a long time with no bible, no book and no catalog entry. She is the
only real second character in the whole library: in five of the seven original
books the companion is an unnamed glow-moth, dragonfly, hedgehog or firefly, and
Nibs is the best of them. Her existence is most of why that book works.
Her defining move is the PUNCTURING QUESTION. In Nibs she asks 'When did you
last actually see it?' and the whole story turns on it. She never lectures, she
never solves anything, and she is usually right early and overruled. Write her
that way or she stops being Tilly.
Her verbal tic is 'Well, now' -- an unhurried opener before she says the thing
that changes everything. She says a character's name first, then pauses.
Her files were Tilly.png / Tilly.webp with a capital T while her id is 'tilly'.
bookCover() derives the path from the id, so she would have 404'd on Vercel the
moment she led a book. Renamed to lowercase to match every other character.
Reference and cover are currently the SAME image, like the seven originals and
unlike Pixie, so a painted title may sit in the generation seed. If she gets a
textless sheet later, split them the way pixie.json describes.
